question: What is the main reason you cancelled your subscription?
study: StreamCo Q3 cancellation survey, n=3,140 open-ends (40 sampled here)

codes.label: Price or value for money
codes.description: The cost was too high, a price rise pushed them out, they were cutting spending, or they judged it not worth what it cost.

codes.label: Not using it enough
codes.description: They rarely opened it, forgot it existed, or their life changed so they no longer had time for it. About frequency of use, not quality.

codes.label: A capability they needed was absent or removed
codes.description: They name something the product does not do, stopped doing, or does worse than they need: offline mode, a device, an export, a plan tier.

codes.label: Technical faults
codes.description: Crashes, freezes, playback or loading failures, errors, things not working on their device. About the software breaking, not about it being confusing.

codes.label: Hard to use or navigate
codes.description: Confusing interface, could not find things, too complicated, bad search or recommendations. The product worked but fighting it was the problem.

codes.label: Customer support experience
codes.description: Slow, unhelpful, rude or absent responses from support, chatbots that went nowhere, or an unresolved complaint.

codes.label: Moved to a competitor
codes.description: They switched to, or already had, a rival service. Naming a competitor or saying they went elsewhere both apply.

codes.label: Content or catalogue quality
codes.description: The library shrank, went stale, lost a title or show they wanted, or the quality of what is offered declined.

codes.label: Billing and renewal handling
codes.description: An unexpected or duplicate charge, a renewal they did not intend, a failed refund, or a cancellation process that obstructed them.

codes.label: Pausing, intending to return
codes.description: They frame the cancellation as temporary: taking a break, pausing over summer, coming back when a show returns.
